caption:
Coca-Cola 2020 buyouts: $7.04B in dividends, 4,000 offered

From the archive: Aug 2020. Not today's news.
Coca-Cola voluntary separation program, 2020: $7.04 billion in dividends paid that year, 4,000 employees first offered a buyout.
Coca-Cola, Aug 28, 2020 (James Quincey, press release): "We have been on a multi-year journey to transform our organization"
Coca-Cola's August 28, 2020 8-K (the filing public companies send the SEC) says the first voluntary separation offers, a buyout where employees choose to leave, will go to about 4,000 employees in the US, Canada and Puerto Rico. Its 2020 10-K (the annual report filed with the SEC) reports $7,047 million in dividends paid.

Same year: $7.04 billion in dividends paid, 2020, company-wide. $7,047 million of dividends paid during 2020, company-wide (Form 10-K).
The math: $7.04 billion in dividends paid, 2020, company-wide ÷ 4,000 employees = $1.76 million in dividends per employee offered a buyout. The result is approximate.
Is a buyout a layoff? No. The 4,000 are the first employees offered voluntary separation, not layoffs. The $7,047 million is dividends paid during 2020, company-wide, per the 10-K.
The facts: $7.04 billion in dividends paid, 2020, company-wide (SEC EDGAR · Coca-Cola, Feb 25, 2021). 4,000 employees will first be offered (SEC EDGAR · Coca-Cola, Aug 28, 2020).

Multi-year journey. Here is the column. (Our take.)

Send this to someone who has been through a round of cuts.

Synthetic voice. Sources: SEC EDGAR · Coca-Cola, Aug 28, 2020; SEC EDGAR · Coca-Cola, Feb 25, 2021.
